population.span: Patients were considered eligible if they had a recent MI ( < 30 days).

endpoint.span: The primary efficacy endpoint was a composite of CV death, resuscitated cardiac arrest, MI, stroke, or urgent hospitalization for angina requiring coronary revascularization.

estimate.span: The primary end point occurred in 5.5% of the patients in the colchicine group, as compared with 7.1% of those in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.61 to 0.96; P = 0.02).

ci.span: The primary end point occurred in 5.5% of the patients in the colchicine group, as compared with 7.1% of those in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.77; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.61 to 0.96; P = 0.02).

treatment_strategy.span: COLCOT was an international multicentre, randomized, double-blinded trial that randomly assigned patients to receive either low-dose colchicine (0.5 mg once daily) or placebo.

follow_up.span: Patients were followed for a median of 22.6 months.

absent_reason: analysis_set: No held source explicitly identifies the analysis population for the overall HR of 0.77. The full-text safety-population statement applies to the separate time-to-treatment analysis.
served_mismatch: The served HR and CI match the overall primary composite reported in the abstract. The served intention-to-treat label cannot be verified from the held sources.

candidate_rejections.span: The present analysis was conducted amongst patients who received at least one dose of the study medication (referred to as the safety population in the main protocol, ) .
candidate_rejections.why: This analysis-set statement belongs to the time-to-treatment analysis and cannot establish the analysis set for the overall HR of 0.77.

candidate_rejections.span: A primary endpoint event occurred in 4.3% of patients in the colchicine group, as compared with 8.3% of those in the placebo group when TTI was between Days 0 and 3 ( N = 1193, HR = 0.52, 95% CI 0.32–0.84, P = 0.007, Figure A ).
candidate_rejections.why: This estimate concerns the Days 0–3 treatment-initiation subgroup, not the overall trial population.

entry_population_matches_question.why: Eligibility specifies adults with myocardial infarction within 30 days; the overall estimate's ITT status remains unstated.
entry_population_matches_question.span: Inclusion Criteria: * Males and females of at least 18 years of age capable and willing to provide informed consent * Patient must have suffered a documented acute myocardial infarction within the last 30 days

notes: Registry evidence is used to confirm adult entry eligibility. Full text supplies trial-level methods, but its subgroup estimates do not replace the overall abstract HR. Follow-up is a median duration, not a fixed assessment timepoint.
